trial_court: Sessions Court at Ankleshwar and District and Sessions Court at Bharuch
case_name: Dipikaben Bhaveshkumar Shah (D/O Vinodkumar Mangaldas Shah) v. Bhaveshkumar Manharlal Shah
facts_of_case: The applicant (wife) seeks transfer of two proceedings initiated by the respondent (husband): Hindu Marriage Petition No. 20 of 2011 seeking divorce and Misc. Civil Application (under Guardian and Wards Act) No. 257 of 2011 for appointing a guardian.

legal_principles.principle: A transfer application may be allowed if the applicant will suffer much more inconvenience and difficulties, besides incurring expenses, if the proceedings are not transferred.
legal_principles.held: The learned advocate for the applicant submitted that, if the aforesaid proceedings have not been transferred as prayed for, the applicant will have to suffer much more inconvenience and difficulties, besides incurring expenses for the same.
cited_cases: Deepti Bhandari Vs. Nitin Bhandari, (2012) 2 GLR 1332

legal_principles.principle: A respondent who is ready and willing to pay the expenses incurred by the applicant for attending proceedings may not be opposed to a transfer application.
legal_principles.held: The learned advocate for the respondent submitted that the respondent is ready and willing to pay the expenses, that may be incurred by the applicant, for attending the aforesaid proceedings filed by the respondent.

outcome.final_order: The application for transfer is allowed.

use_for_drafting: guiding principles for family law disputes
strategies for transferring cases between courts
